items.conditions: Natural unit of time built from fundamental constants (sqrt(hbar G / c^5)); the scale below which current physics cannot describe time. Not an observed event.
items.conditionsFr: Unite de temps naturelle construite a partir des constantes fondamentales (racine de hbar G / c^5) ; echelle en dessous de laquelle la physique actuelle ne sait plus decrire le temps. Ce n'est pas un evenement observe.
items.locator: NIST CODATA value page 'Planck time', Numerical value line
items.confidenceNotes: CODATA 2022 recommended value. Standard uncertainty 0.000 060 x 10^-44 s, relative standard uncertainty 1.1 x 10^-5 (dominated by the uncertainty of G). Derived constant, not a measured duration of any process.

items.labelFr: Duree de vie moyenne du muon (au repos)
items.conditions: Average lifetime of a muon at rest before it decays (mostly into an electron and two neutrinos). Muons created by cosmic rays live longer as seen from the ground because of relativistic time dilation.
items.conditionsFr: Duree de vie moyenne d'un muon au repos avant sa desintegration (surtout en electron et deux neutrinos). Les muons crees par les rayons cosmiques vivent plus longtemps vus du sol, a cause de la dilatation relativiste du temps.
items.locator: PDG 2024 Summary Tables, Leptons, mu block, page 1
items.confidenceNotes: PDG 2024 world average of experimental measurements; uncertainty ±0.0000022e-6 s (about 1 ppm). Value stored in microseconds (2.1969811 us = 2.1969811e-6 s). | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: reference value restated by the source, no protocol published there: classified documented.

items.labelFr: Duree de vie moyenne du neutron libre
items.conditions: Average lifetime of a neutron outside an atomic nucleus before it decays into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino (about a quarter of an hour). Neutrons bound in stable nuclei do not decay.
items.conditionsFr: Duree de vie moyenne d'un neutron hors d'un noyau atomique avant sa desintegration en proton, electron et antineutrino (environ un quart d'heure). Les neutrons lies dans des noyaux stables ne se desintegrent pas.
items.locator: PDG 2024 Summary Tables, Baryons, n block (N baryons)
items.confidenceNotes: PDG 2024 average, uncertainty ±0.5 s already inflated by scale factor S = 1.8, which PDG uses when input measurements are mutually inconsistent. The measurements of this quantity are known to disagree between experimental methods (the 'neutron lifetime puzzle'); the size of that discrepancy was not sourced here, so treat the last digit with caution. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: reference value restated by the source, no protocol published there: classified documented.

items.conditions: Time for half of a sample of carbon-14 atoms to decay into nitrogen-14; the clock behind radiocarbon dating.
items.conditionsFr: Temps au bout duquel la moitie des atomes de carbone 14 d'un echantillon se sont desintegres en azote 14 ; c'est l'horloge de la datation au radiocarbone.
items.locator: LNHB Table de Radionucleides C-14, section 2 'Nuclear Data', page 1
items.confidenceNotes: DDEP/LNHB recommended value 5700 a with standard uncertainty 30 a (notation '(30)'). Radiocarbon laboratories conventionally report ages with the older 'Libby' half-life of 5568 a; that convention was not sourced here and is not this value. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: reference value restated by the source, no protocol published there: classified documented.

items.conditions: Time for half of a sample of uranium-238 to decay (mainly by alpha emission); about the age of the Earth, which is why U-238 is used to date the oldest rocks.
items.conditionsFr: Temps au bout duquel la moitie d'un echantillon d'uranium 238 s'est desintegree (surtout par emission alpha) ; c'est a peu pres l'age de la Terre, d'ou son usage pour dater les roches les plus anciennes.
items.locator: LNHB Table de Radionucleides U-238, section 2 'Nuclear Data', page 1
items.confidenceNotes: DDEP/LNHB recommended value 4.468 x 10^9 a, standard uncertainty 0.005 x 10^9 a. The quote is copied from the PDF text layer where the superscript of 10^9 is flattened to '109' and the French decimal comma is used. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: reference value restated by the source, no protocol published there: classified documented.

items.labelFr: Temps de trajet de la lumiere Terre-Lune (distance moyenne)
items.conditions: Time for light (or a radio signal) to cross the mean Earth-Moon distance (semimajor axis 384 400 km), one way. Low/high: Moon at perigee (363 300 km) and apogee (405 500 km).
items.conditionsFr: Temps mis par la lumiere (ou un signal radio) pour parcourir la distance moyenne Terre-Lune (demi-grand axe 384 400 km), aller simple. Bas/haut : Lune au perigee (363 300 km) et a l'apogee (405 500 km).

calculation.formula: t = d / c (d (semimajor axis) = 3.844e+08 m; d (perigee) = 3.633e+08 m; d (apogee) = 4.055e+08 m; c = 2.99792e+08 m/s; c = 299 792 458 m/s)

items.locator: NASA Moon Fact Sheet, orbital parameters table (Semimajor axis, Perigee, Apogee rows)
items.confidenceNotes: Calculated: 384 400 000 m / 299 792 458 m/s = 1.2822 s (perigee 1.2118 s, apogee 1.3526 s), rounded to 1 ms. Centre-to-centre distances; real surface-to-surface signal paths are slightly shorter. The '106' in the quote is the fact sheet's 10^6 with its superscript flattened. Perigee/apogee values carry an asterisk on the fact sheet (footnote not read).

items.labelFr: Temps de trajet de la lumiere Soleil-Terre (distance moyenne)
items.conditions: Time for sunlight to reach Earth at the mean Sun-Earth distance (Earth's orbital semimajor axis, 149.598 million km): about 8 min 19 s. Low/high: Earth at perihelion (early January) and aphelion (early July).
items.conditionsFr: Temps mis par la lumiere du Soleil pour atteindre la Terre a la distance moyenne (demi-grand axe de l'orbite terrestre, 149,598 millions de km) : environ 8 min 19 s. Bas/haut : Terre au perihelie (debut janvier) et a l'aphelie (debut juillet).

calculation.formula: t = d / c (d (semimajor axis) = 1.49598e+11 m; d (perihelion) = 1.47095e+11 m; d (aphelion) = 1.521e+11 m; c = 2.99792e+08 m/s; c = 299 792 458 m/s)

items.locator: NASA Earth Fact Sheet, orbital parameters (Semimajor axis, Perihelion, Aphelion rows)
items.confidenceNotes: Calculated: 149 598 000 000 m / 299 792 458 m/s = 499.005 s (perihelion 147.095e9 m -> 490.66 s; aphelion 152.100e9 m -> 507.35 s), rounded to 0.1 s. The IAU 2012 exact astronomical unit (149 597 870 700 m) would give the same value to 0.1 s, but the IAU resolution PDF could not be opened (HTTP 404/502), so the NASA semimajor axis is used. Month names for perihelion/aphelion are general knowledge, not read on the source; remove if strictness requires.

items.labelEn: Earth sidereal day (rotation relative to the stars)
items.labelFr: Jour sideral terrestre (rotation par rapport aux etoiles)
items.conditions: Time for Earth to turn once relative to distant stars: about 23 h 56 min, roughly 4 minutes shorter than the 24 h solar day because Earth also moves along its orbit.
items.conditionsFr: Temps mis par la Terre pour faire un tour par rapport aux etoiles lointaines : environ 23 h 56 min, soit a peu pres 4 minutes de moins que le jour solaire de 24 h, car la Terre avance aussi sur son orbite.
items.locator: NASA Earth Fact Sheet, 'Sidereal rotation period (hrs)' row
items.confidenceNotes: Fact-sheet value given to 4 decimals of an hour (~0.2 s resolution); no uncertainty stated. Earth's rotation varies by milliseconds over days to decades, far below this precision. Same sheet gives 'Length of day (hrs) 24.0000' for the mean solar day. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: reference value restated by the source, no protocol published there: classified documented.

items.conditions: Time between two successive identical seasonal points (e.g. spring equinox to spring equinox); the year calendars try to follow.
items.conditionsFr: Temps entre deux retours successifs au meme point des saisons (par exemple d'un equinoxe de printemps au suivant) ; c'est l'annee que les calendriers cherchent a suivre.
items.locator: NASA Earth Fact Sheet, 'Tropical orbit period (days)' row
items.confidenceNotes: Given to 3 decimals of a day; no uncertainty stated. Distinct from the sidereal year (365.256 d on the same sheet), which is measured against the stars; the difference comes from the precession of Earth's axis. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: reference value restated by the source, no protocol published there: classified documented.

items.labelEn: Synodic month (new Moon to new Moon)
items.labelFr: Mois synodique (d'une nouvelle Lune a la suivante)
items.conditions: Average time between two identical Moon phases (e.g. full Moon to full Moon). The orbit measured against the stars (sidereal) is shorter: 27.3217 d.
items.conditionsFr: Temps moyen entre deux phases identiques de la Lune (par exemple d'une pleine Lune a la suivante). L'orbite mesuree par rapport aux etoiles (siderale) est plus courte : 27,3217 j.
items.locator: NASA Moon Fact Sheet, orbital parameters, 'Synodic period (days)' row
items.confidenceNotes: Mean value, 2 decimals, no uncertainty stated. Individual lunations vary by several hours around the mean (amount not sourced here). The 27.3217 d sidereal figure is the 'Revolution period (days)' row of the same sheet. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: reference value restated by the source, no protocol published there: classified documented.

items.labelFr: Periode orbitale de la comete de Halley
items.conditions: Time for comet 1P/Halley to go once around the Sun; last closest approach to the Sun (perihelion) on 1986-02-09.
items.conditionsFr: Temps mis par la comete 1P/Halley pour faire le tour du Soleil ; dernier passage au plus pres du Soleil (perihelie) le 9 fevrier 1986.
items.locator: NASA Comet Fact Sheet, row '1P Halley', column 'Orbital Period (yrs.)'
items.confidenceNotes: Osculating period for the 1986 apparition; the period changes from one passage to the next because of planetary perturbations and outgassing (range not sourced here). Quote reassembled from table cells split across lines in the page text. Sheet last updated 2016. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: reference value restated by the source, no protocol published there: classified documented.

items.conditions: Time for Jupiter to orbit the Sun once relative to the stars (sidereal period): about 11.86 Earth years.
items.conditionsFr: Temps mis par Jupiter pour faire le tour du Soleil par rapport aux etoiles (periode siderale) : environ 11,86 annees terrestres.
items.locator: NASA Jupiter Fact Sheet, 'Sidereal orbit period (days)' row (Jupiter column)
items.confidenceNotes: No uncertainty stated. The row lists Jupiter, Earth and the Jupiter/Earth ratio (11.862). Tropical period on the same sheet: 4,330.595 d. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: reference value restated by the source, no protocol published there: classified documented.

items.labelEn: Sun's orbit around the centre of the Milky Way ('galactic year')
items.labelFr: Orbite du Soleil autour du centre de la Voie lactee (« annee galactique »)
items.conditions: Approximate time for the Sun (and the Solar System) to complete one trip around the centre of our Galaxy.
items.conditionsFr: Temps approximatif mis par le Soleil (et tout le Systeme solaire) pour faire un tour complet autour du centre de notre Galaxie.
items.locator: NASA 'Our Sun: Facts', section 'Orbit and Rotation'
items.quote: it takes about 230 million years for the Sun to make one complete trip around the Milky Way.
items.confidenceNotes: Rounded order-of-magnitude estimate ('about'); depends on the adopted Sun-centre distance and circular speed. An independent popular source, NRAO 'Ask an Astronomer' (J. Mangum, 2015, src-nrao-galactic-orbit), states 'about 226 million years'. Other published estimates spread further (roughly 220-250 Myr in secondary press found during search) but no primary paper was opened, so low/high are left null rather than invented. Low confidence on any digit beyond the first two.

items.conditions: Time since Earth and the other solid bodies of the Solar System formed, determined from lead isotopes in Earth's oldest lead ores and in meteorites.
items.conditionsFr: Temps ecoule depuis la formation de la Terre et des autres corps solides du Systeme solaire, determine a partir des isotopes du plomb des plus vieux minerais terrestres et des meteorites.
items.locator: USGS 'Geologic Time: Age of the Earth', final paragraphs
items.quote: an age for the Earth and meteorites, and hence the Solar System, of 4.54 billion years with an uncertainty of less than 1 percent.
items.confidenceNotes: USGS states uncertainty below 1 % (i.e. under about ±0.045 billion years); no exact interval given, so low/high left null. Page last updated 2007; it summarises Dalrymple (1991). The same page gives a meteorite formation span of 4.53-4.58 billion years. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: reference value restated by the source, no protocol published there: classified documented.

items.conditions: Time since the Big Bang inferred from the Planck satellite's map of the cosmic microwave background, assuming the standard cosmological model (base Lambda-CDM), combined with lensing and baryon acoustic oscillation data.
items.conditionsFr: Temps ecoule depuis le Big Bang, deduit de la carte du fond diffus cosmologique du satellite Planck, en supposant le modele cosmologique standard (Lambda-CDM de base), combine aux donnees de lentillage et d'oscillations acoustiques des baryons.
items.locator: Planck 2018 VI, Table 2, row 'Age [Gyr]', column TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO
items.confidenceNotes: 68 % interval ±0.020 Gyr (13.787 ± 0.020 x 10^9 a). Model-dependent inference, not a direct measurement: the Planck-only baseline (TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing) gives 13.797 ± 0.023 Gyr in the same table, and the 'Hubble tension' (disagreement between early- and late-Universe H0 values) means a different model could shift the age; not quantified here. Quote abridged with '...' between table columns. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: reference value restated by the source, no protocol published there: classified documented.
